title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Accounting and Finance (2017)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Accounting and Finance (2017). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: Equipment purchased on January 01, 2021, for birr 80,000 was depreciated using the straight-line method based upon a 5-year life and birr 7,500 residual value. The equipment was sold on December 31, 2023, for birr 40,000. What is the gain on the sale of the equipment?
questions.explanation: Annual depreciation = (80,000 - 7,500)/5 = 14,500 birr per year. Accumulated depreciation after 3 years (2021, 2022, 2023) = 14,500 × 3 = 43,500 birr. Book value at time of sale = 80,000 - 43,500 = 36,500 birr. Gain on sale = Selling price - Book value = 40,000 - 36,500 = 3,500 birr.

questions.questionText: Which of the following events would generally be classified as non-operating on an enterprise fund statement of revenues, expenses, and changes in net assets?
options: Loss on the sale of a piece of equipment
questions.explanation: Loss on sale of equipment is a non-operating item because it is not related to the primary, ongoing operations of the enterprise. Depreciation, customer account expenses, and administrative expenses are all considered operating expenses as they relate to the regular business activities.

questions.questionText: Which of the following characteristics of dividend payable is different from other current liabilities?
options: It is a result of advance service receipt
It is a result of long term liabilities
It is a result of board of directors authorization
It is a result of advance cash receipt
questions.explanation: Dividends require board authorization.

questions.questionText: The date of the auditor's opinion on the financial statements of the client should be the date of the
options: finalization of the terms of the audit engagement
completion of all important audit procedures
submission of the report to the client
questions.explanation: Auditor's opinion date aligns with completion of audit procedures.

questions.questionText: Compared to the plant wide rate method, activity-based costing usually shifts costs from
questions.explanation: Activity-based costing (ABC) typically shifts costs from high-volume to low-volume products when compared to traditional plant-wide overhead allocation methods. This occurs because ABC allocates overhead based on specific cost drivers and activities rather than a single volume-based measure. Low-volume products often consume disproportionately more resources per unit, which traditional costing methods fail to capture, causing high-volume products to subsidize low-volume products.

questions.questionText: Financial regulation demonstrates
options: financial regulation makes the market to promote continence in the company's internal inefficiency and fairness of their activities
financial regulation may be applied to facilitate the general operation of markets, to enhance safety or to pursue social objectives
financial regulation on depositors as well as financial instructions especially banks make them protected how their own financial failure
financial regulation gives room for more monopolies
questions.explanation: Financial regulation serves to facilitate markets and social objectives.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is identified as the business function used for sales class of transaction in the sales and collection cycle?
options: Processing and recording sales return and allowance
questions.explanation: Granting credit is part of the sales cycle.

questions.questionText: A firm has a degree of financial leverage of 5.5; what does this tell us about the firm?
options: If sales rise by 5.5% then EBIT will rise by 1%
If sales rise by 1% then EPS will rise by 5.5%
If EBIT rise by 1% then EPS will rise by 5.5%
If EBIT rise by 5.5% then EPS will rise by 1%
questions.explanation: The Degree of Financial Leverage (DFL) measures the sensitivity of earnings per share (EPS) to changes in earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT). A DFL of 5.5 means that a 1% change in EBIT will result in a 5.5% change in EPS. This high leverage indicates the firm has significant fixed financial costs like interest expenses.

questions.questionText: In exchanges of asset in which the exchange has commercial substance:
options: Losses, but not gains, are recognized immediately
Neither gains nor losses are recognized immediately
Both gains and losses are recognized immediately
Gains, but losses, are recognized immediately
questions.explanation: Both gains and losses are recognized in commercial substance exchanges.

questions.questionText: When evaluating mutually exclusive projects, it's best to choose the one with the:
questions.explanation: When evaluating mutually exclusive projects (where only one can be chosen), the project with the highest Net Present Value (NPV) should typically be selected as it represents the greatest increase in shareholder wealth. While IRR is also important, it can sometimes lead to incorrect decisions when projects have different scales or timing of cash flows. In cases where NPV and IRR give conflicting recommendations, NPV should generally be preferred as the primary criterion.

questions.questionText: A successor would most likely make specific inquiries of the predecessor auditor about which one of the following?
options: Specialized accounting principles of the client's industry
The competency of the client's internal audit staff
Disagreements with management as to auditing procedure
The uncertainty inherent in applying sampling procedure
questions.explanation: Successor inquires about disagreements with management.

questions.questionText: What is the main function of stock market:
options: Simplifying companies to raise capital by selling shares
questions.explanation: Stock markets facilitate capital raising via shares.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about unsystematic risk?
options: Can be effectively eliminated by portfolio diversification
Is compensated for by the risk premium
questions.explanation: Unsystematic risk (also called diversifiable or firm-specific risk) can be effectively eliminated through portfolio diversification. Unlike systematic risk (market risk), which affects the entire market and is measured by beta, unsystematic risk is specific to individual companies or industries and can be reduced by holding a diversified portfolio of assets.

questions.questionText: Liquidity preference theory stated that:
options: More liquid asset offer higher potential returns
Less liquid asset are generally more liquid
There is no relationship between liquidity and return
Investment prioritize liquidity over higher returns
questions.explanation: Liquidity preference theory, developed by Keynes, states that investors generally prefer to hold liquid assets and will demand a premium (higher return) for investing in less liquid assets. This means investors often prioritize liquidity over higher returns, requiring additional compensation to give up liquidity. This explains why long-term investments typically offer higher yields than short-term ones.

questions.questionText: Which of the following journal entry applied to record the payment of salaries to employees of sales agency?
options: Salary expense sales-agency debited and credited to cash
Agency working capital/ agency imprest fund debited and credited to cost of goods sold
Agency working capital/ agency imprest fund debited and credited to salary expense sales-agency
Salary expense sales agency debited and credited Agency working capital/ agency imprest fund
questions.explanation: Debit Salary Expense, credit Cash.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the opportunity of the security market development in Ethiopia?
options: Good public confidence in share investment
The development of private sector is low
The public awareness about securities market is too high
questions.explanation: Unexploited resources present opportunities.

questions.questionText: All of the following are categories of income exempted from employment income tax, except:
options: Pension, provident fund and all other retirement benefit (up to 15% of the monthly salary of employee)
Casual employees (who do not work under the same employer for more than one month in a year)
Gratitude in relation to the death of another person
questions.explanation: Basic salary is taxable.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following should be done to the book value of the old equipment in a decision to retain or replace equipment? Treating as a (an):
questions.explanation: The book value of old equipment is a sunk cost in replacement decisions. Sunk costs are past costs that cannot be recovered and should be irrelevant to future decisions. In equipment replacement analysis, only the future cash flows (like potential salvage value) should be considered, not the remaining book value of the existing equipment.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statement is/are not true about public and private finance?
options: The pattern of expenditure of an individual is governed by habits, customs, status, personal needs, whereas the pattern of public expenditure is governed and controlled by deliberate economic policy of the government
Government cannot use coercive methods to raise his income, whereas an individual can use forceful methods to collect revenue
Private cannot use coercive methods to raise his income, whereas an Government can use forceful methods to collect revenue
The government has a right to print currency which is legal, whereas individual dose not enjoy such a right
questions.explanation: The statement that 'Government cannot use coercive methods to raise income, whereas individuals can use forceful methods' is false. In reality, governments have taxation powers and legal authority to enforce collection (coercive methods), while individuals cannot legally use force to collect revenue. Options A, C, and D are all correct statements about differences between public and private finance.

questions.questionText: Nuna Company, a public limited company, has granted 100 share appreciation rights of its 10 employees on 1 July 2011. This is classified under:
options: Share-based payment transaction with cash alternative
questions.explanation: Share appreciation rights are cash-settled.

questions.questionText: Which of the following accounts is unique to a merchandising business compared to a service based business?
questions.explanation: Merchandise inventory is unique to merchandising.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following long-term sources of fund for commercial bank?
questions.explanation: Bank capital is a long-term source.

questions.questionText: Which of the following describes costs that change proportionately with volume?
questions.explanation: Variable costs vary with volume.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is categorized as deductible temporary difference?
options: Prepaid expense that are deducted on the tax return in the period paid
Sales accounted for on the accrual basis for financial reporting purpose and on the installment (cash) basis for tax purposes
Investment accounted for under the equity method for financial reporting purposes and under the cost method for tax purposes
Bad debt expense recognized using the allowance method for financial reporting purposes: direct write-off method used for tax purposes
questions.explanation: Bad debt expense using the allowance method creates a deductible temporary difference. Under the allowance method (accounting), expenses are recognized when estimated before actual defaults occur, while under the direct write-off method (tax), expenses are only recognized when accounts actually become uncollectible. This timing difference creates a deductible temporary difference, as the book expense precedes the tax deduction, resulting in a future tax benefit (deferred tax asset).

questions.questionText: Mutual fund pool investor money to invest in:
options: Providing insurance coverage for individual assets
questions.explanation: Mutual funds invest in diversified assets.

questions.questionText: Unrealized gains or losses of debt investment held for collection and selling is reported on:
options: Other comprehensive income and as a separate component of equity
On profit or loss statement and as a separate component of equity
questions.explanation: Reported in OCI for debt investments held for collection.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not source of revenue assigned to federal government in Ethiopia?
options: Taxes collected from income generated through air, rail, and sea transport services
Profit and sales taxes collected from individual traders operating within state/regional government territories
Income tax collected from employees of federal government and international organizations
Taxes collected from national lotteries and other games of chance
questions.explanation: In Ethiopia's federal system, profit and sales taxes collected from individual traders operating within state/regional territories are assigned to state/regional governments, not the federal government. The federal government's revenue sources include taxes from international transportation (air, rail, sea), income taxes from federal and international organization employees, and national lottery taxes, as mentioned in the other options.

questions.questionText: Which of the following documents and records is applied for cash disbursements class of transaction in acquisition and payment cycle?
questions.explanation: Checks or electronic payments document disbursements.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is considered a general long-term liability except:
questions.explanation: Treasury bills are short-term government securities, typically with maturities of one year or less, and therefore are not considered general long-term liabilities. Claims and judgments, pension obligations, and bonds/notes are all examples of long-term liabilities as they typically extend beyond one year.

questions.questionText: When should a receivable be recognized in the financial statements?
options: When the goods or services are delivered to the customer
When cash is received from the customer
When the invoice is issued to the customer
When the payment terms of the receivable expire
questions.explanation: Recognized upon delivery (revenue recognition principle).

questions.questionText: All of the following are a common source of financing for major acquisitions of general capital assets to be accounted for in capital project funds except:
options: Issuance of long-term debt to be repaid from tax revenues
questions.explanation: Proprietary and fiduciary funds are not typically sources for financing capital projects accounted for in capital project funds. Proprietary funds are used for business-type activities that are self-supporting, while fiduciary funds hold resources in trust for others. Neither is commonly used to directly finance general government capital acquisitions. The other options (long-term debt, gifts, and transfers from other funds) are all common financing sources for capital projects.

questions.questionText: When a company has a foreign subsidiary, which of the following exchange rates is typically used to translate the subsidiary's financial statements into the reporting currency?
questions.explanation: When translating foreign subsidiary financial statements, the average exchange rate for the period is typically used for income statement items (revenues, expenses) to reflect the rates throughout the period when transactions occurred. Balance sheet items are typically translated at the current/closing rate (spot rate), except for equity accounts which use historical rates. Forward rates are used for hedging transactions, not for financial statement translation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statement demonstrates the transaction related audit objectives of completeness for acquisitions of good and service transaction?
options: Recorded acquisitions are for good and service received, consistent with the best interests of the client
questions.explanation: The completeness objective ensures that all existing transactions are recorded.

questions.questionText: An extraordinary item differs from a special item in that an extraordinary item is:
options: Usual in nature and frequent in occurrence
Reported on a separate line below general revenues
Unusual in nature and infrequent in occurrence
questions.explanation: Extraordinary items are both unusual in nature and infrequent in occurrence, distinguishing them from special (or unusual) items which may be either unusual OR infrequent, but not necessarily both. Note: Under updated GAAP and IFRS standards, the 'extraordinary items' classification has been eliminated, but the conceptual distinction remains important for understanding financial statement analysis.

questions.questionText: The legal agreement that specifies the terms and provisions of the business combination is termed as:
questions.explanation: A merger agreement is the legal document that outlines the terms of a business combination.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statement states the importance independent audit to readers of financial statements?
options: Measures and communicates financial and business data included in financial statements
Involves the objective examination of and reporting on management-prepared statements
Reports on the accuracy of all information in the financial statements
Shows stewardship of the company's management whose financial statements are audited
questions.explanation: Independent audits provide objective examination of management-prepared financial statements.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statement best describes the method used in indirect method to prepare statement of cash flow
options: It starts with net cash flow and converts in to net income
It starts with net income and converts in to net cash flow
It deducts operating cash disbursements from operating cash receipts
It is the presentation of a condensed cash receipts and cash disbursements statement
questions.explanation: The indirect method starts with net income and adjusts it to arrive at net cash flow from operations.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is responsible for auditing taxpayer's returns to determine whether they have complied with the tax laws?
questions.explanation: Internal revenue agents are responsible for auditing tax returns for compliance with tax laws.

questions.questionText: According to the IASB conceptual framework, which of the following enhances the comparability of financial information?
questions.explanation: Consistency in accounting methods enhances comparability of financial information over time.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a money market security?
questions.explanation: Treasury bills are short-term money market securities.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a disadvantage of the corporate form of organization?
questions.explanation: The separation of ownership (shareholders) from management can be a disadvantage of the corporate form as it may lead to agency problems where management's interests differ from those of shareholders. This separation can result in higher agency costs and potential conflicts of interest. The other options represent advantages of the corporate form: easier capital raising through stock issuance, continuous existence independent of owners, and limited liability protection for shareholders.

questions.questionText: What are the three types of business entities?
questions.explanation: The three main types of business entities are proprietorships, partnerships, and corporations.

questions.questionText: The current ratio is
options: Calculated by dividing current liabilities by current assets
Used to evaluate a company's solvency and long-term debt paying ability
Used to evaluate a company's liquidity and short-term debt paying ability
Calculated by subtracting current liabilities from current assets
questions.explanation: The current ratio measures a company's liquidity and short-term debt paying ability by comparing current assets to current liabilities. It is calculated by dividing current assets by current liabilities, not the reverse. A ratio greater than 1 indicates that a company has more current assets than current liabilities, suggesting better short-term financial health.

questions.questionText: Intangibles may arise from the following sources except
options: Private monopolistic arrangements arising from contractual agreements, such as franchises and leases
Government grants, such as patents, copyrights, licenses, trademarks, and trade names
Acquisition of another business, in which the purchase price includes a payment for goodwill
Intangible assets not arise from anywhere and not to be considered as assets on the report
questions.explanation: Intangible assets do arise from identifiable sources and should be reported as assets.

questions.questionText: Which of the following dividend policies involves paying a fixed amount of dividends per share, irrespective of the company's earnings?
questions.explanation: A stable dividend policy involves paying a fixed or steadily increasing dividend amount per share regardless of earnings fluctuations. Companies following this policy prioritize dividend consistency to provide shareholders with reliable income streams, even if earnings temporarily decline. This contrasts with a residual dividend policy (paying dividends from leftover funds after investments) or a compromise policy (balancing stability and proportion to earnings).

questions.questionText: How is goodwill calculated in the consolidated financial statements on the date of acquisition?
options: It is calculated as the difference between the subsidiary's book value and the fair value of its net assets
It is calculated as the difference between the parent's book value and the fair value of its investment in the subsidiary
It is calculated as the excess of the consideration transferred over fair value of the subsidiary's identifiable net assets
It is calculated as the excess of the subsidiary's net income over the parent's net income
questions.explanation: Goodwill equals the purchase price minus the fair value of identifiable net assets acquired.

questions.questionText: Which of the following definition is applied for directed sample selection in audit sampling?
options: sample in which every possible combination of elements in the population has an equal chance of constituting the sample
probabilistic method of sampling in which the auditor calculates an interval and selects the items for the sample based on the size of the interval
non-probabilistic method of sample selection in which items are chosen without regard to their size source, or other distinguishing characteristics
non-probabilistic method of sample selection in which each items in the sample is selected based on some judgmental criteria established by the auditor
questions.explanation: Directed (or judgmental) sample selection is a non-probabilistic method where the auditor selects items based on specific judgmental criteria rather than random selection. This approach allows auditors to focus on items they believe have higher risk or particular characteristics meriting examination. Unlike statistical sampling methods (described in options A and B), directed sampling doesn't provide a statistical basis for conclusions about the entire population.

questions.questionText: In a company which uses job order costing when a job is completed, which entry is made to show the completion of the job?
options: Debit to cost of goods sold birr and credit to finished goods inventory
Debit to finished goods inventory and credit to raw material inventory
Debit to accounts receivable birr and credit to sales
Debit to finished goods inventory and credit to work in process inventory
questions.explanation: Completion of a job transfers costs from work in process to finished goods inventory.

questions.questionText: In which one of the methods for arranging business combinations a new corporation is formed to issue its common stock for the outstanding common stock of two or more existing corporations?
questions.explanation: A statutory consolidation creates a new corporation that acquires two or more existing companies.

questions.questionText: Which one of the governmental funds is used to account for legally restricted resources provided by trust in which the earnings but not the principal may be used for purposes that support the primary government's programs?
questions.explanation: Permanent funds account for resources where only earnings, not principal, can be spent.

questions.questionText: A current asset financing policy under which the working capital is primarily financed by long-term sources
questions.explanation: A conservative policy uses long-term financing for working capital needs.

questions.questionText: What is the defensive tactics that a target company in a hostile takeover to resists the proposed business combination through amendment of the articles of incorporation or bylaws to make it more difficult to obtain stockholder approval for a takeover?
questions.explanation: Poison pill strategies make a company less attractive to hostile acquirers.

questions.questionText: The market based measure of allocating joint costs of production method, which one the following works award in that the overall gross profit rate is computed first?
questions.explanation: The constant gross-margin percentage NRV (net realizable value) method first calculates the overall gross profit percentage for all joint products, then allocates costs to achieve this same gross profit percentage for each product. This differs from other methods like the sales value at split-off (which uses relative sales values at the split-off point) or physical measures method (which allocates based on physical attributes like weight or volume).

questions.questionText: In audit sampling for test of control and substantive test of transactions, selecting the sample is performed in
options: Select the sample and perform the audit procedures step
questions.explanation: Sample selection occurs during the 'select and perform' phase of audit sampling.

questions.questionText: What does the term 'debit' indicate in accounting?
questions.explanation: Debits increase asset accounts in the accounting equation.

questions.questionText: A segment of Tora Inc. has the following data. Sales birr 500,000 variable costs birr 340,000 fixed costs birr 200,000 if this segment is eliminated, 50% of the fixed costs will be eliminated and the rest will be allocated to the remaining segments. What should Troa do?
options: Eliminate the segment; net loss will be birr 60,000 lesser
Keep the segment; net loss will be birr 100,000 lesser
Eliminate the segment; net loss will be birr 100,000 lesser
Keep the segment; net loss will be birr 60,000 lesser
questions.explanation: Segment contribution = Sales - Variable costs = 500,000 - 340,000 = 160,000 birr. If eliminated: Fixed costs saved = 200,000 × 50% = 100,000 birr. Net benefit of keeping segment = Contribution - Avoidable fixed costs = 160,000 - 100,000 = 60,000 birr. Therefore, keeping the segment reduces the net loss by 60,000 birr compared to eliminating it.

questions.questionText: The capital market facilitates the trading of:
questions.explanation: Capital markets deal with long-term securities like stocks and bonds.

questions.questionText: When a partnership interest is purchased
options: The transaction is a personal transaction between the purchaser and the selling partner(s)
All partners will receive some part of the purchase price
Buyer receives equity equal to the amount of cash paid
Every partner's capital account is affected
questions.explanation: Purchasing a partnership interest is a personal transaction between buyer and seller.

questions.questionText: A form of taxation that is basically imposed on the services given to individuals through offing scales on documentation is known as
questions.explanation: Stamp duties are taxes on legal documents and transactions.

questions.questionText: Income taxes currently payable is
questions.explanation: Income taxes currently payable represents the actual tax obligation for the current period that must be paid to tax authorities. This differs from income tax expense (which includes both current and deferred components), and deferred tax liabilities (which represent future tax obligations due to temporary differences between accounting and tax treatments).

questions.questionText: The bond investment which is hold for trading strategy is measured by
options: Both amortized cost and equity method
questions.explanation: Trading securities are measured at fair value with changes recognized in earnings.

questions.questionText: In using the percentage of sales forecasting method the assumption is that:
options: There is a direct relationship between long-term debt and sales
Contributed capital will increase proportionality with sales
Inventories will increase proportionality with sales
There is a direct relationship between notes payable and sales
questions.explanation: The percentage of sales forecasting method assumes that many balance sheet items, including inventories, will vary directly and proportionally with sales. As sales increase, items like accounts receivable, inventory, and certain current liabilities are expected to increase at the same rate. However, long-term debt and contributed capital (options A and B) typically don't have this direct proportional relationship with sales, as they're influenced by separate financing decisions.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following costs is classified as a period cost for a manufacturing?
questions.explanation: Tax accountant salary is a period cost (administrative expense) rather than a product cost.

questions.questionText: How profits or losses treated in joint operation?
options: The party has no right on the profit or losses of the joint arrangement
Each party has a share in the profit or loss relating to the activities of the arrangement
Each party has a share in the profit but not loss relating to the activities of the arrangement
Each party receive an allocation of revenues and expenses based on the relative performance of each party to the joint arrangement rather than profit or loss
questions.explanation: In a joint operation, each party recognizes its share of both profits and losses related to the activities of the arrangement, in accordance with IFRS 11. Joint operators recognize their share of assets, liabilities, revenues, and expenses in the joint arrangement. This is different from a joint venture where parties recognize only their interest in the net assets through equity accounting.

questions.questionText: When preparing consolidated financial statements on the date of acquisition, how are the assets and liabilities of the acquired company typically recognized?
options: At fair value on the acquisition date
questions.explanation: Acquired assets and liabilities are recognized at fair value in acquisition accounting.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about the focus of governmental financial reporting except
options: Ongoing ability to raise taxes and manage resources
questions.explanation: Net income is not a primary focus of governmental financial reporting.

questions.questionText: What is the main purpose of the miller and Orr model?
options: To identify the optimal level for cash balance with uncertainty
To predict the likelihood of bankruptcy
To determine the optimal time to invest in a project
To determine a firm's optimum cash balance with certainty
questions.explanation: The Miller-Orr model helps determine optimal cash management policies under conditions of uncertainty and cash flow variation. Unlike the Baumol model (which assumes constant and predictable cash flows), Miller-Orr establishes upper and lower control limits for cash balances, with rules for when to buy or sell securities to adjust cash levels. It's designed for realistic business environments where cash inflows and outflows are irregular and unpredictable.

questions.questionText: Which inventory classification represents goods on hand purchased for resale by a retailer?
questions.explanation: Retailers hold merchandise inventory for resale to customers.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statement describes the percentage-of-completion method in the long-term contract revenue?
options: Recognizes revenue only to the extent of costs incurred that are expected to be recoverable
It accumulates progress billing in an inventory account
Recognizes revenues, costs, and gross profit as a company makes progress toward completion
It accumulates construction costs in an inventory account
questions.explanation: Percentage-of-completion recognizes revenue based on progress toward completing the contract.

questions.questionText: Using the following information: Direct materials standard cost 5 kg * birr 2 per kg = birr 10; Total direct materials variance: birr 15,000 unfavorable; Actual direct materials used: 300,000; Actual units produced: 60,000 units. Compute the total actual cost of direct materials used
questions.explanation: Standard cost per unit = 10 birr. Total standard cost for 60,000 units = 60,000 × 10 = 600,000 birr. Since the variance is 15,000 birr unfavorable, the actual cost exceeds the standard by this amount. Therefore, actual cost = 600,000 + 15,000 = 615,000 birr.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following wrong about taxation?
options: Taxation has insignificant effect on consumption and employment pattern
Tax imposes duty of payment on person who is liable to it
Taxes are compulsory payments to the government
Tax receipts are commonly used for the production of public goods
questions.explanation: Taxation significantly affects consumption patterns and employment decisions.

questions.questionText: Which accounting standard specifies the criteria for recognizing and measuring impairment losses on assets?
questions.explanation: IAS 36 (Impairment of Assets) specifies the procedures and criteria for recognizing, measuring, and disclosing impairment losses on assets. It requires that assets should not be carried at more than their recoverable amount and establishes when and how to perform impairment tests. The other standards have different focuses: IAS 38 covers intangible assets, IFRS 9 deals with financial instruments, and IAS 16 addresses property, plant, and equipment.

questions.questionText: Miami solar budgets production of 5,000 solar panels in July, each unit requires 4 hours of direct labor at a rate of $ 16 per hour, prepare a direct labor costs?
questions.explanation: Direct labor cost = Number of units × Hours per unit × Rate per hour = 5,000 solar panels × 4 hours × $16 per hour = 20,000 hours × $16 = $320,000 (or birr 320,000, assuming the currency conversion is 1:1 for this problem).

questions.questionText: A security $150 per year in perpetuity. What is its present value today, given that the required rate of return is 4.75 percent?
questions.explanation: For a perpetuity (cash flow that continues forever), the present value formula is: PV = Annual payment / Discount rate. In this case: PV = $150 / 0.0475 = $3,157.89. This represents the sum of all future payments discounted at 4.75% per year.

questions.questionText: Which of the following costs should be debited to an expense account and not included in the total cost of a fixed asset?
questions.explanation: Costs due to carelessness or error should be expensed rather than capitalized.

questions.questionText: Which standard of IFRS is used for treatment of the agricultural produce growing on the bearer plant asset?
questions.explanation: IAS 41 (Agriculture) governs the accounting treatment for agricultural produce growing on bearer plants. While the bearer plants themselves (such as grape vines or tea bushes) are accounted for under IAS 16 (Property, Plant and Equipment), the produce growing on these plants (grapes, tea leaves) is treated as a biological asset under IAS 41 and measured at fair value less costs to sell. IFRS 16 covers leases, and IFRS 15 addresses revenue from contracts.

questions.questionText: The conflict of interest between stockholders and management is known as
questions.explanation: The agency problem describes conflicts between principals (owners) and agents (managers).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not party involved on the check?
questions.explanation: Brokers are not parties to a check transaction (maker, payee, and payer are).

questions.questionText: Which of the following statement explains the transaction-related audit objectives of accuracy for sales transaction?
options: Sales are recorded on the correct dates
Recorded sales are for shipments actually made to no fictitious customers
Recorded sales are for the amount of goods shipped and are correctly billed and recorded
questions.explanation: Accuracy means sales are recorded for correct amounts and properly billed.

questions.questionText: In which of the following engagements an auditor provides a limited level of assurance that the information subject to review is free of material misstatements?
questions.explanation: Reviews provide limited assurance, unlike audits which provide reasonable assurance.

questions.questionText: Identify the requirements not used in the joint arrangement formation?
options: Contractual arrangement about its amount of tax paid
Contractual arrangement about its activity, duration and reporting obligations
Contractual arrangement about the appointment of its B.O.Ds (or equivalent) & the voting rights of the parties
Agreement about the capital contribution to it by the parties
questions.explanation: Tax arrangements are not a required element in forming a joint arrangement.

questions.questionText: National Bank of Ethiopia as a Regulator of financial system do?
options: Create favorable conditions for the expansion of banking, insurance and other financial services
License and supervise banks, insurers and other financial institutions
Make short term and long-term refinancing facilities
questions.explanation: The National Bank of Ethiopia, as a regulator, both creates favorable conditions for financial services expansion (A) and licenses and supervises financial institutions (B).

questions.questionText: If the contribution margin percentage is 30%, the selling price is $5000, then the contribution margin per unit will be?
questions.explanation: Contribution margin per unit = Selling price * Contribution margin percentage = $5000 * 30% = $1,500.

questions.questionText: It is the date on which the entity and another party agree to a share-based payment arrangement?
questions.explanation: The grant date is when the entity and the counterparty agree on the terms of the share-based payment.

questions.questionText: The private organization responsible for establishing the standards for financial accounting and reporting in the United States is called?
options: American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA)
questions.explanation: The FASB is responsible for establishing accounting standards in the U.S.

questions.questionText: Within the government-wide financial statements, the column for Business-type Activities will generally include?
questions.explanation: Business-type activities are typically represented by enterprise funds.

questions.questionText: A review of any part of an organization's procedures and methods for the purpose of evaluating efficiency and effectiveness is classified as a(n)?
questions.explanation: An operational audit evaluates the efficiency and effectiveness of an organization's operations.

questions.questionText: According to IAS41 Agriculture, which one of the following items would be classified as biological assets?
questions.explanation: Trees are classified as biological assets under IAS 41 as they are living organisms capable of biological transformation.

questions.questionText: Proprietary fund category is made up of?
options: Internal service fund and Expendable trust fund
Enterprise fund and Expendable trust fund
Enterprise fund and Internal Service fund
Internal service fund and Special Revenue fund
questions.explanation: Proprietary funds consist of enterprise funds and internal service funds.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about management accounting?
options: It is based on a set of generally accepted accounting principles
questions.explanation: Management accounting focuses on future-oriented reports for internal decision-making.

questions.questionText: When we develop predetermined overhead rate the base should be best cost driver. The underlined phrase implies that?
options: The base inversely related to consumption of overhead cost
Consumption of overhead cost greater than actual
Consumption of overhead less than actual
The base positively related to consumption of overhead cost
questions.explanation: The base should be positively related to the consumption of overhead costs.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an argument against regulation?
options: Promote foreign participants in the domestic market
Curb the failure of financial institutions
questions.explanation: Regulation can create moral hazard by encouraging riskier behavior.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a goal of financial regulation?
options: Ensuring the soundness of the financial system
questions.explanation: All listed options are goals of financial regulation.

questions.questionText: What entities shall apply IFRS 11?
options: Only those entities that have joint control over a joint arrangement
Only those entities that have significant influence over a joint arrangement
Only those entities that are a party to a joint arrangement
questions.explanation: IFRS 11 applies to all entities that are a party to a joint arrangement, regardless of whether they have joint control.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements about capital markets and securities are true?
options: The maturity of a debt instrument is the time (term) to that instrument's expiration date.
debt instrument is long term if its maturity is ten years or longer.
bond is a long-term security that promises to make periodic payments called dividends to the firm's residual claimants.
questions.explanation: Statements A and B are true regarding capital markets and securities.

questions.questionText: __________ Bonds protect a business against dishonest employees.
questions.explanation: Fidelity bonds protect businesses against losses caused by dishonest employees.

questions.questionText: Which of the following terms are defined by the statement: 'The currency of the primary economic environment in which the entity operates'?
questions.explanation: Functional currency is the currency of the primary economic environment in which the entity operates.

questions.questionText: A form used to appeal raw material from the store to the production center is known as?
questions.explanation: A Material Requisition form is used to request raw materials from the store.

questions.questionText: A debit balance in which of the following accounts would indicate a likely error?
questions.explanation: A debit balance in Fees Earned indicates an error, as it should have a credit balance.

questions.questionText: A group of manufacturing costs referred to as prime costs include?
questions.explanation: Prime costs consist of direct materials and direct labor.
